Dear Mr. Parent:
At your request, I have reviewed the records of Thomas Hughes. My understanding is that the
purpose of this review was to determine if there was any medical evidence of incapacity to make
decisions regarding his property at the time of signing a new will in September 2022. I was also asked to
comment on his vulnerability to undue influence at that time. Mr. Hayes passed away on January 2,
2023, at the age of 97. To complete this review, I was provided with medical records, bates-stamped
Hughes 1000-1299. Some of these records were illegible.
What follows is a brief summary of my review to date. If additional information becomes
available, I will amend my report as necessary.
Summary:
Throughout his life, Mr. Hughes had been a high level government employee with no history of
mental illness. At the time of his death he was living with his wife. In the last years of his life, Mr.
Hughes
suffered
from
multiple
chronic
illnesses,
including
amongst
others,
pulmonary
disease, hypertension and chronic diarrhea and fatigue. He also had a history of bladder cancer. In the
final years of his life, he required assistance with bathing, dressing and ambulation.
Apart from a hospitalization in February 2021, there are no references in his records to any
mental disorders or dementia. During the February 2021 hospitalization, there was documentation of
probable delirium or confusion while he was treated for a bowel obstruction. However, this confusion did
not persist and was not noted in subsequent medical records. A review of his ongoing medications in
2022 revealed no prescriptions for mental disorders or dementia. The majority of his medications were
long-standing and not known to cause confusion. There are no medical notes from September 2022
indicating any cognitive concerns. Additionally, there are multiple notes of correspondence or telephone

Parent/Thomas Hughes: February 12, 2025
Page 2 of 2
calls between Mr. Hayes and his doctors in the late summer and fall of 2022 that do not suggest any
cognitive complaints. In November 2022, Mr. Hughes experienced a seizure, which was a new onset issue
for him at the time. He died in early January 2023.
Opinion:
My opinion, to a reasonable degree of medical certainty and based on the information provided to
date, is that Thomas Hughes was not suffering from any medical or psychiatric disorder in September
2022 that would have significantly impaired his capacity to manage his property. While he was physically
debilitated, there was no evidence in the provided record of being overly or increasingly dependent or
reliant on others to meet his needs.
I trust this addresses your concerns. Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions.
Sincerely,
Christiane Tellefsen, M.D.

Time is of the essence. Per MD Code Ann. E&T 3-407, Mrs. Hughes is required to make her
election of the elective share by the later of either nine (9) months after Mr. Hughes' death or six

Personal Representative on January 26, 2023. Thus, any election must be filed by October 26,

ascertain whether it is in Mrs. Hughes' interest to make an elective share election. Please confirm

II.
Notice of Petition to Caveat Will and Petition for Court to Assume Jurisdiction of
Trust
Mrs. Hughes intends to challenge the September 26, 2022 Last Will and Testament of Thomas
Lowe Hughes ("Will") and the Trust of Thomas Lowe Hughes ("Trust") for which you serve as
Trustee. We are in the final stages of preparing a Petition to Caveat the Last Will and Testament
of Thomas Lowe Hughes. Mrs. Hughes also intends to ask the Orphans' Court to assume
jurisdiction over the Trust. Mrs. Hughes paid $750,000 for Mr. Hughes' benefit so that he could
reacquire a 50% interest in the title to the Western Ave. Property that was previously transferred
to Carleton College. She paid the money so that she would either have the right to live in a
cooperative housing unit in Mr. Hughes' name located at 3583 Hamlet Pl ., Chevy Chase, MD
("Hamlet P1. Property") for the remainder of her life (life estate) or secure, outright, the shares of
for the unit. We understand that following Mr. Hughes' death, title to the Western Ave. Property
was transferred to the Trust and that title to the shares of the Hamlet Place Property were
transferred to Carleton College. We further understand that you intend to sell the Western Ave.
Property and that Carleton College intends to sell the shares to the Hamlet Pl. Property.

Bradford T. Nordholm, Trustee

Thus, the estate plan that you are implementing, and which was developed in September 2022, is
not in line with what Mrs. Hughes understood she and her husband intended. What Mr. and Mrs.
Hughes planned was that upon Mr. Hughes' death, Mrs. Hughes would receive either title to the
shares of the Hamlet Pl. Property or receive the right to live there until her death (a life estate), so
that should she need assistance, her children would be able to assist her, in her home, without any
negative impact on her or them financially or emotionally. The Hamlet Pl. Property would
adequately fit her personal items and accommodate her and her children. That is why she paid
Carleton College money to see that 50% of the title in Western Ave. Property was returned to Mr.
Hughes. She would not have done so had she known that she would be disinherited and dumped
into an assisted living facility. Indeed, we have records showing that Mrs. and Mr. Hughes
expressly rejected the use of revocable trusts in their estate plans. We also believe that Mr. Hughes
lacked testamentary capacity and/or was unduly influenced when he executed estate documents in
September 2022 and that those documents to not reflect Mr. Hughes' intent vis a vis the disposition
of his property. We intend to bring all our concerns involving the Will and the Trust to the Court's
attention. Once Mrs. Hughes files the Petition to Caveat, you will be stripped of authority to act
as Personal Representative of the Estate and you convert to a Special Administrator. Once the
Court assumes jurisdiction over the Trust, your actions as Trustee/Successor Trustee will be
scrutinized by the Court and we will expect that all distributions of Trust assets to beneficiaries
will cease until Mrs. Hughes' claims are resolved. Please confirm.
III. Demand for Return of Personal Property

Western Ave. Property of all personal items. Many of the personal items which were removed
from the home belonged to Mrs. Hughes. To add insult to injury, you told Mrs. Hughes' daughter

remaining items in the Western Ave. Property - clothes - and that you have refused to move the
clothes for Mrs. Hughes, thereby expecting an 85 year old woman, mourning the loss of her
husband and recovering from recent breast cancer surgery to either abandon the property or collect
it by herself. That is unreasonable. All of Mrs. Hughes' property needs to be returned to her
immediately, at the Trust's expense and without any impact on Mrs. Hughes. Please confirm you
will do so and that none of the property will be disposed of without express written authority. If
it is not returned to her, we intend to seek the assistance of the Court.

Dear Mr. Parent:
I write in response to your letter of June 16, 2023. I appreciate your courtesy in awaiting
a response as I completed my arbitration.
With respect to the central premise of your letter, that Mrs. Jane Hughes, provided me with
instructions to discontinue all actions in connection with the will caveat initiated on her behalf,
suffice it to say, we have serious doubts Ms. Hughes knowingly drafted the email/communication
you referenced. We suspect that someone either drafted it for Mrs. Hughes or manipulated her to
do so as Mrs. Hughes is, now, highly susceptible to undue influence, for a variety of reasons, and
likely has diminished competence. We intend to find out who was responsible for the email
through discovery and will report same to the Court at the proper time. Regardless, several care
providers working with Mrs. Hughes have already expressed concern about Mrs. Hughes' mental
state to Mrs. Reid. We are following up on those concerns. Should the review impact the case in
any way, we will let you know.
Beyond that, however, we would be remiss if we did not tell you how troubling your letter
is to us, and not because you baselessly threaten to seek sanctions. What is so troubling about your
communication is that Mrs. Hughes' electronic "communications" with others are either making
their way to you, or being read by others with whom you have connections, for you to use as a
basis to threaten us and Mrs. Hughes' daughter with sanctions under the Maryland Rules. Mrs.
Reid, who oversees Mrs. Hughes' finances and property pursuant to a validly executed Power of

Attorney, and who maintains a very close relationship with her mother, was unaware that Mrs.

that not only did you somehow gain access to Mrs. Hughes' communications, but that you thought
the best use of her private information was to threaten me and Mrs. Reid with sanctions.
So that you are aware, we do not assume that you communicated directly with Mrs. Hughes.
That would be an obvious ethical violation. What we do believe, however, is that one or more of
your clients did, and continue to do so, and that you likely learned of Mrs. Hughes'
communications through your client(s) who likely did have access to Mrs. Hughes and her
communications. Afterall, Mr. Nordholm refused to accept my instruction that he should not
communicate with me and likely pressed Mrs. Hughes for information, and we understand his wife
pays regular visits to Mrs. Hughes in her current residence. We do not see it as a coincidence that
following these communications and visits, Mrs. Hughes wrote me an email that only benefits your
client(s), and that shortly thereafter, you wrote to me threatening sanctions, an act which similarly .
only benefits your client(s).
These facts, coupled with the context of your letter make clear that your assumption - that
Mrs. Hughes is competent to make all decisions vis a vis her estate and property - is flawed.
According to you, Mrs. Hughes is competent to make decisions with respect to her affairs,
independently sent an email to me about the case, and then knowingly directed her
communications to you or to whomever informed you of the email so that her communications
could be used as a basis to threaten her daughter with sanctions. I am sure you will agree with me,
that conclusion defies all reason. Mrs. Hughes had no reason to see her daughter threatened with
sanctions. She has a very loving and caring relationship with her daughter. If she did not want
litigation, it is highly unlikely she would want her daughter sanctioned in that litigation. Yet that
is precisely how you used Mrs. Hughes' communication. We can only conclude, therefore, that
Mrs. Hughes' communications made their way to you, either directly or indirectly, because Mrs.
Hughes did not know or was unable to prevent her communications from being directed to you
and used against her daughter.
I am sure you will agree with me that, if that is what happened, as we suspect, such behavior
is reprehensible and not something the Court will countenance when the behavior is revealed, as
it looks little more than a scheme to manipulate someone with diminished competency to suppress
facts from being conveyed to the Court. But, beyond that, and to the extent that the email Mrs.
Hughes wrote to me was redirected to you or accessed by someone with whom you have a
connection, without Mrs. Hughes' knowing authority, such conduct would violate federal, District
of Columbia, and Maryland law. We trust that you have advised whoever forwarded the email to
you (or who accessed it to tell you about the communication) accordingly and instructed that
person immediately to discontinue their access to Mrs. Hughes' electronic communications. We
intend to investigate the matter, but to avoid any concerns that your client(s) may be involved with
manipulating Mrs. Hughes or accessing her communications without her permission, you should
advise them to stay away from Mrs. Hughes until this matter is resolved, effective immediately.
Please confirm you will do so. If not, then we will assume that the potential for additional
interference continues and will seek appropriate relief as may be necessary.

COMPLAINT FOR DECLARATORY JUDGMENT AND FOR DAMAGES
Jane Casey Hughes, by and through her Attorney-in-Fact Carolina Reid, through her
counsel, Jesse D. Stein and Selzer Gurvitch Rabin Wertheimer & Polott, PC, hereby submits this
Complaint for Declaratory Judgment and for Damages, and in support thereof states:
I.
Parties
1.
Plaintiff Jane Casey Hughes is an individual who currently resides in an assisted living
facility in Washington, D.C. At all times relevant hereto, however, Ms. Hughes was a resident of
the State of Maryland who lived in Chevy Chase, Maryland. It is believed and further alleged that
(00597273;1 }

Mrs. Hughes is incompetent due to dementia and is unable to manage her affairs independently
and that she was incompetent and unable to manage her affairs during the events described herein.
Until he died on January 3, 2023, Mrs. Hughes was married to Thomas Lowe Hughes ("Mr.
Hughes").
2.
Carolina Reid is an adult resident of the State of Texas who resides at the address listed
above. Ms. Reid is Mrs. Hughes' daughter and serves as Mrs. Hughes' Attorney-in-Fact pursuant
to a valid Power of Attorney which, inter alia, authorizes and empowers her to take legal action on
behalf of her mother. She brings this Complaint for Declaratory Judgment and for Damages in her
representative capacity of Mrs. Hughes, the real party in interest in this dispute.
3.
Carleton College ("Carleton") is a Minnesota Nonprofit Corporation located in Northfield,
Minnesota at the address set forth above. As explained herein, Carleton was involved in a
transaction which should be declared void due to the fact that the donor, Mr. Hughes, lacked
capacity when the transaction at issue - a gift of shares of a cooperative housing unit located in
Chevy Chase, Maryland worth approximately $844,000 was made from Mr. Hughes to Carleton.
4.
Brad Nordholm ("Nordholm") is an adult resident of the State of Maryland who resides at
the address set forth above. He is Mr. Hughes' nephew. It is believed and further alleged that
Nordholm, with the help of others, orchestrated the gifting of the cooperative housing units at issue
in this matter from Mr. Hughes to Carleton when Mr. Hughes lacked capacity to either execute
testamentary documents or formulate the necessary donative intent to make a gift of property to
any person or entity.
{00597273;1 }2

II.
Jurisdiction
5.
This Court has personal jurisdiction over the Defendants pursuant to MD Code 6=102 and
6-203 in that Nordholm is a resident of the State of Maryland and that the events described herein
occurred in the State of Maryland.
6.
Venue is proper in Montgomery County, Maryland pursuant to MD Code 6-202 in that the
causes of action described below arose in Montgomery County, Maryland in that when they
occurred, Mr. Hughes and Mrs. Hughes lived in Montgomery County, Maryland.
III.
Facts Common to All Counts
7.
Mrs. Hughes incorporates herein the foregoing facts as if fully set forth.
8.
Mrs. Hughes and Mr. Hughes married in 1995. It was the second marriage for each. Prior
to marrying Mr. Hughes, Mrs. Hughes sold her home in the District of Columbia and at marriage,
moved into Mr. Hughes' home located on Western Avenue, Chevy Chase, MD ("Western Ave.
Property").
9.
In addition to owning the Western Ave. Property, Mr. Hughes owned shares of a cooperative
housing unit located on Hamlet Pl ., Chevy Chase, MD ("Hamlet Pl."). By December 2022, Mr.
Hughes' interest in Hamlet Pl. was worth at least $884,000.
10.
Contemporaneous with the marriage, Mr. and Mrs. Hughes signed an antenuptial
agreement, which provided, in pertinent part, that neither had any claim to the other's property
upon the death of the first spouse to die.
11. Mr. Hughes was an alumnus of Carleton and, at some point, he decided he wished to make
a gift to Carleton. Mr. Hughes decided that he wished to give Carleton a share of the Western Ave.
(00597273;1 }3

Property. In 1996, he executed a Special Warranty Deed which deeded to Carleton College a 50%
tenant in common interest in the Western Ave. Property subject to the contingent life estate interest
of Mrs. Hughes.
12.
In 2010, consistent with that intent, Mr. Hughes executed his Last Will and Testament
("2010 Will") which provided, inter alia:
I previously transferred one-half of my interest in my residence located at 5653 Western
Avenue, Chevy Chase, Maryland ("Western Avenue Residence") to Carleton College while
retaining a life estate for myself and granting a contingent life estate to JANE if she
survived me; JANE subsequently executed a deed whereby she relinquished said
contingent life estate. I hereby direct my Personal Representative to work with Carleton
College to sell my remaining interest in my Western Ave Residence as soon as practicable
after my death; providing that I JANE survives me, my Personal Representative shall allow
her ample time to arrange for the storage, sale or transfer of her personal property there. It
is my desire that the sale of my Western Avenue Residence be accomplished within two
years of my death, but I grant my Personal Representative full authority and discretion to
accomplish the sale upon the terms and conditions and within he timelines as they
determine are in the best interest of my estate and my beneficiaries hereunder. JANE shall
be under no obligation to pay rent while she resides or has access to my residence after my
death. Any and all expenses of maintaining my Western Avenue Residence prior to sale
shall be paid by my estate without recourse against JANE. Upon the sale of thr Western
Avenue Residence, all of the net sale proceeds attributable to my interest shall be
distributed as part of my residuary estate under Item Third hereof.
Notwithstanding any provision or interpretation of my Prenuptial Agreement with JANE
to the contrary, I further direct that my Personal Representative transfer outright all of my
interest in my townhouse at 3555 Hamlet Place, Chevy Chase, Maryland, and all of my
contents, fixtures and equipment located therein, along with the sum of ONE HUNDRED
THOUSAND DOLLARS ($100,000) to my wife JANE, if she survives me, but if not, said
items shall be distributed as part of my residuary estate under item THIRD hereof.
13. Mr. Hughes did not utilize a trust in connection with this 2010 estate plan. Instead, he left
the remainder of his residuary estate to his children if they survived him.
14.
In 2017, Mr. Hughes executed a Deed as the "sole owner as to an undivided 50% interest
in the Property" which, in exchange for $750,000, transferred to Mr. Hughes all of Carleton interest
in the Western Ave. Property. As a result of the 2017 Deed, Mr. Hughes became the sole owner of
the title to the Western Ave. Property.
(00597273;1 )4

15. Mr. Hughes borrowed the money to purchase Carleton's interest in the Western Ave.
Property from Mrs. Hughes. The loan was not repaid.
16. The sole purpose of the March 2017 transaction from Mrs. Hughes' perspective, however,
was not to secure Mr. Hughes a 100% interest in the Western Ave. Property. In 2017, Mr. Hughes
was 90 and Mrs. Hughes was 78 years old. Mrs. Hughes and Mr. Hughes knew that there was a
chance Mr. Hughes would predecease Mrs. Hughes and the parties wished to establish an estate
plan which ensured that Mrs. Hughes would have a place to live should Mr. Hughes predecease
Mrs. Hughes, as was likely given the age difference between the parties.
17.
The antenuptial agreement notwithstanding, Mr. and Mrs. Hughes developed joint estate
plans, which, among other things, left property, and rights to the surviving spouse between them.
18.
In other words, even thought Mr. and Mrs. Hughes signed an antenuptial agreement, they
abandoned and/or modified and/or amended the agreement by subsequent conduct and writings
which developed and revised estate plans wherein they left property and rights to the surviving
spouse upon the first to die.
19. Between 1995 and January 3, 2023, Mr. and Mrs. Hughes each revised estate documents
at least three (3) times and in each case, they continued to ensure that each received property and
rights from the other upon the first of them to die.
20.
The will at issue in this case was a Last Will and Testament that Mr. Hughes executed in
2019 ("2019 Will"). At the time and for the preceding 25 years, Mr. and Mrs. Hughes lived in Mr.
Hughes' home located on Western Ave. in Chevy Chase, MD. Mr. Hughes purchased the home
with his first wife, who died in 1991, so the 2019 Will provided that upon his death, the Western
Ave. Property was to be sold, but that before it was sold, Mrs. Hughes was entitled to live in the
(00597273;1 ) 5

Western Ave. Property for as long as she wished while she arranged for the disposition of her
property in the Western Avenue property.
21. Further, and critically for purposes of this Complaint, the 2019 Will provided that Mr.
Hughes' interest in Hamlet Pl. was to pass to Mrs. Hughes upon his death.
22.
Specifically, the 2019 Will stated:
I direct the sale of my Western Avenue home as soon after my death as practicable, this
transaction to completed within one year of my death, if possible. But I grant my Personal
Representatives full authority and discretion to accomplish the sale upon the terms and
conditions and within such timeframes as they determine are in the best interest of my
estate and my beneficiaries hereunder.
Provided, however, that if JANE survives me, she is allowed ample time to arrange for the
disposition of her personal property in the Western Avenue house. Until such time she may
continue to live there free of any rental obligation. All costs of maintaining that residence
or preparing it for sale shall be paid as expenses of administration of my estate.
Since the original purchase of the Western Avenue residence in 1967, my family has
benefitted so greatly from the foresight and ingenuity of my first wife JEAN in locating
and furnishing said residence, I desire to maximize the proceeds from the sale of sale
residence to benefit both of our sons EVAN and ALLAN. Hence the residue of my estate
(including any property over which I may have testamentary power or control) shall be
divided into equal shares: one share to each then surviving son of mine, each such share to
be distributed outright to such son; provided further that if my son EVAN predeceases me,
but is survived by his wife Lynn McCary Hughes (hereinafter LYNN), who also survives
me, then LYNN shall receive that otherwise would have gone to EVAN hereunder had he
survived me.
I direct that my full interest in my Hamlet Place co-op go to JANE, outright and free of
trust, if she survives me. If she does not survive me, it should be added to my residue of
my estate.
23.
Mr. Hughes was twelve years (12) years older than Mrs. Hughes and by 2022, Mr. Hughes
began to suffer cognitive and physical decline. By 2022, Mrs. Hughes, who herself was suffering
from cognitive impairments and physical ailments cared for Mr. Hughes around the clock.
24.
Mr. Hughes was so cognitively and physically impaired, that by 2022, Nordholm was
handling transactions for Mr. Hughes as he could not conduct them himself.
{00597273;1 }6

25. Mr. Hughes, it is believed, had a Durable Power of Attorney which appointed Mrs. Hughes
as his primary Attorney-in-Fact and Nordholm as Mr. Huges' Successor Attorney-in-Fact. By
2022, however, both Mr. and Mrs. Hughes were so incapacitated that Nordholm bypassed Mrs.
Hughes as Mr. Hughes' Attorney-in-Fact and acted as Mr. Hughes' Attorney-in-Fact without Mrs.
Hughes' help.
26. In 2022, Nordholm, with the assistance of others, such as Marc Johannessen
("Johannessen") from Creative Planning, LLC, Mr. and Mrs. Hughes' financial planner, and
possibly others, contrived a plan to allow Mr. Hughes to make a substantial gift to Carleton while
preserving the Western Ave. Property for Mr. Hughes' children. The plan involved gifting Hamlet
Pl. to Carleton, regardless of the fact that the 2019 Will provided that Hamlet Pl. was to pass to
Mr. Hughes' wife, Mrs. Hughes and regardless of the fact that Mr. Hughes lacked testamentary
capacity and the capacity necessary to formulate a donative intent.
27.
Beginning in 2022, Nordholm and others influenced Mr. Hughes to execute new estate
documents, including a will ("2022 Will") and a Revocable Trust ("Trust"). It took a very long
time for Nordholm and others like Johannessen to convince Mr. Hughes to execute the estate
documents because he did not understand and/or lacked the capacity necessary to execute estate
documents in 2022. Mrs. Hughes does not believe that Mr. Hughes, who in September 2022 was
over 96 years old and cognitively and physically impaired could comprehend the estate plan others
prepared for him or appreciate the significance of the dispositive provisions of the 2022 Will or
how his assets would be managed in the Trust.
28. Mr. Hughes executed the new estate documents on September 26, 2022, at a time when Mr.
Hughes was unable to formulate the testamentary capacity necessary to execute estate documents
such as the 202 Will and the Trust document. Nonetheless, Mr. Hughes, due to the influence of
{00597273:1 ) 7

others like Nordholm and Johannessen, executed the 2022 Will and Trust and thereby radically
changed his estate plan, essentially, leaving his beloved second wife, Mrs. Hughes, without any
rights in Mr. Hughes' estate. It was a radical departure from Mr. Hughes' prior estate plans which
expressly provided for Mrs. Hughes to make sure she had a place to live should Mr. Hughes
predecease her.'
29.
The 2022 Will left nothing to Carleton, either.
30.
Mr. Hughes died on January 3, 2023. A mere ten (10) days before he died, however, he,
with the assistance of others, including but not limited to Nordholm and, possibly Mr. and Mrs.
Huges' joint attorney Aen Webster, purportedly gifted his interest in Hamlet Pl. to Carleton.
31. At the time of the "gift"/transfer, Mr. Hughes lacked the capacity necessary to formulate
donative intent and the gift was not a product of his free will. Mrs. Hughes believes that Nordholm,
who is also an alumnus of Carleton and who now sit on the Carleton Board of Trustees (since
2023) orchestrated the gift to Carleton notwithstanding the fact that Mr. Hughes lacked the capacity
necessary to effectuate the gift. Petitioner believes that Nordholm received his appointment to
Carleton's Board of Trustees, in part, due to the gift from Mr. Hughes of Hamlet Pl.
32. As explained below, as a direct and proximate cause of Nordholm's and other's actions,
Mrs. Hughes has been harmed and as a result, either the gift of the shares of Hamlet Pl. should be

inheritance from Mr. Hughes failed.
